Card Summary: Contraindication of medication for patient allergy: {{ActualMedication}} with allergen {{ActualAllergen}}.
Card Detail: The use of {{RuleMedication}} is contraindicated when the patient has an allergy to NSAIDs. It is recommended to avoid prescribing any NSAID for this patient.

{{RuleMedication}} is formulated as a lipid emulsion containing purified egg phosphatide, so it has traditionally been avoided in patients allergic to {{RuleAllergen}}. Current evidence does not support an absolute contraindication: egg allergy is usually to ovalbumin in egg white, while the lecithin in propofol comes from yolk. Confirm what the reaction was before substituting, and have resuscitation available if there is a history of anaphylaxis.

{{RuleMedication}} emulsion contains refined soybean oil, which is the reason it is often flagged against allergy to {{RuleAllergen}}. Refined soybean oil is essentially protein-free and a controlled study found no link between propofol allergy and soy allergy. Routine avoidance is not evidence based; proceed and monitor as usual.

Methylprednisolone sodium succinate preparations use lactose of bovine origin as an excipient, and trace cow's milk proteins have been detected in every batch tested. Anaphylaxis has been reported after intravenous dosing in children with severe allergy to {{RuleAllergen}}. Check the excipients of the specific preparation before giving a parenteral corticosteroid; oral prednisolone tablets are not implicated.
